Expected win probability from two Elo ratings

Source: R/elo_expected.R
elo_expected.Rd

Calculates the probability that player A beats player B, based only on the gap between their Elo ratings, using the standard logistic Elo formula \(E_A = 1 / (1 + 10^{(R_B - R_A) / scale})\). A 0-point gap gives 0.5; a player rated 200 points higher wins about 76% of the time.

Usage

elo_expected(rating_a, rating_b, scale = 400)

Arguments

rating_a

Numeric. Elo rating(s) for player A.

rating_b

Numeric. Elo rating(s) for player B. Must be the same length as rating_a, or length 1.

scale

Numeric. Rating gap that produces 10-to-1 odds. Defaults to 400, the standard chess value.

Value

A numeric vector of probabilities between 0 and 1 that player A wins.

Examples

# Equal ratings give a 50% chance
elo_expected(1500, 1500)
#> [1] 0.5

# A 200-point favorite wins about 76% of the time
elo_expected(1700, 1500)
#> [1] 0.7597469

# Vectorized over several matchups
elo_expected(c(1600, 1800, 2000), 1700)
#> [1] 0.3599350 0.6400650 0.8490204
